rj_bouillon_sainte.intro: Water, salt and minerals against dehydration, and warmth for the whole body.
etapes: The blanching: bring the water to the boil and add the stock cube.
The sacrifice: plunge the nettles and herbs into the simmering broth. Cooking removes the nettle's sting in under a minute.
The reduction: let it simmer 10 minutes over the embers, until the leaves are very tender.
The crushing: off the heat, crush the leaves against the side with a spoon.
Serving: piping hot in your mug, before an effort or before sleeping.
attention: Only pick what you identify with certainty (see the species sheets), away from roads, treated fields and places where dogs go.
Sorrel: rich in oxalic acid, eat it in moderation, and avoid it if you have kidney stones.

ingredients: 1 handful of nettle tops (picked with gloves or a bag)
1 handful of dandelion or wild sorrel leaves, identified with certainty
1 vegetable stock cube
400 ml of water

rj_bouillon_sainte.source: Original Bivaska recipe, inspired by Elden Ring and Dark Souls. Unofficial: Bivaska is not affiliated with or endorsed by any publisher of the games mentioned

rj_brocheton_pirate.intro: Lean protein, and a morale bonus for the whole camp.
etapes: The weapon: cut a long, thin green hazel branch. Strip the bark from the last 15 centimetres and carve a point.
The skewering: thread alternately a piece of fish or chicken, a petal of onion and a square of bacon.
The lock: leave a knot in the branch or cut a notch at the base so nothing slides off.
The cooking: hold the skewer 20 cm above the embers and turn it often: the bacon fat melts and coats the flesh.
The timing: 12 to 15 minutes. The onion should blacken at the edges, and the meat be cooked through.
attention: Poultry and pork must be cooked through: cut the biggest piece, the flesh must no longer be pink and the juices must run clear.
Cod holds badly on a branch: use thick cubes, or chicken.

recette.jeu: Sea of Thieves and Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag
ingredients: 1 fillet of firm white fish (cod, pollock) or 1 chicken breast, in large cubes
½ onion in wide petals
1 slice of smoked bacon in squares
Salt, pepper

rj_brocheton_pirate.source: Original Bivaska recipe, inspired by Sea of Thieves and Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag. Unofficial: Bivaska is not affiliated with or endorsed by any publisher of the games mentioned

rj_pemmican.intro: Maximum energy density: protein, fat and berries in a small block.
etapes: The powder: at home, crush or blend the dried meat into a coarse powder, like sawdust.
The binder: add the crushed berries.
The blend: pour in the melted fat, warm but not hot, then knead until you get a very dense, even paste.
The mould: shape small balls or spread the paste out to cut into bars.
Storage: let it set somewhere cool, then wrap it in baking paper. Dry and cool, it keeps several weeks.
attention: Use shop-bought, thoroughly dry dried meat: pemmican only keeps if everything is perfectly dry. Throw it away if it smells rancid or turns damp.
Very fatty and very filling: a few mouthfuls are enough.

recette.cuisson: No cooking in the field (prepared at home)
ingredients: 50 g of shop-bought dried meat (beef jerky), ground to a powder
50 g of lard, beef tallow or clarified butter (ghee), melted
30 g of dried berries (cranberries, blueberries), crushed

rj_pemmican.source: Original Bivaska recipe, inspired by RimWorld and The Oregon Trail. Unofficial: Bivaska is not affiliated with or endorsed by any publisher of the games mentioned

rj_pochee_espace.intro: A hot meal in 5 minutes, with almost no washing-up.
etapes: The crushing: without opening the noodle packet, crush it between your hands to break the noodles into small pieces.
The loading: pour the noodles, the dried soup and the drained fish into your mug or mess tin.
The reactor: cover with boiling water, a centimetre above the food.
The containment: close with the lid and wedge it between two stones, or in a hat, to keep the heat in for 5 minutes.
The extraction: stir and eat, with chopsticks carved from dead wood if you have no spoon.
attention: Don't pour boiling water into the noodle packet: it isn't made for that, it warps and can burn your fingers. Only freeze-dried meal pouches are designed for boiling water.

ingredients: 1 packet of instant noodles (ramen type)
1 sachet of dried soup (vegetable or miso)
1 small tin of tuna or crab meat
Boiling water

rj_pochee_espace.source: Original Bivaska recipe, inspired by The Outer Worlds and Starfield. Unofficial: Bivaska is not affiliated with or endorsed by any publisher of the games mentioned

rj_etouffee_trappeur.intro: Melt-in-the-mouth meat cooked in its own steam, easy to digest.
etapes: The mattress: spread out a double layer of foil.
The bed: put the onion and garlic in the centre.
The coating: coat the meat with mustard, lay it on the onions, salt and pepper.
The braise: close an airtight dome-shaped parcel, leaving a little air for the steam.
The burial: dig a hollow in the hot ashes at the foot of the fire, put the parcel in and cover with ash and a few embers. 25 to 30 minutes without touching it.
The check: open it and cut the biggest piece. If it's still pink, close it and put it back for 10 minutes.
attention: Poultry and pork must be cooked through: cut the biggest piece, the flesh must no longer be pink and the juices must run clear.

recette.cuisson: In a foil parcel under the ash
ingredients: 1 chicken breast (or shop-bought rabbit fillet) in large strips
½ onion, sliced
1 garlic clove, sliced
1 tablespoon of strong mustard (in a mini tube)
Salt, pepper
Aluminium foil

rj_etouffee_trappeur.source: Original Bivaska recipe, inspired by World of Warcraft. Unofficial: Bivaska is not affiliated with or endorsed by any publisher of the games mentioned

rj_kari_sud.intro: Spices warm you up and mask the taste of purified water.
etapes: The spicy base: pour the sardine oil into the hot mess tin and toast the curry for 30 seconds over the embers.
The liquid: add the coconut milk and mix well. Bring to a simmer.
The plunge: add the whole sardines and the rice (or the crackers to thicken).
The simmering: 5 to 7 minutes over a very gentle heat, at the edge of the fire.
Serving: an adventurer's dish, rich and fragrant, in the middle of the cold forest.
attention: Curry burns quickly: 30 seconds is enough, otherwise it turns bitter.

ingredients: 1 small carton of coconut milk (200 ml)
1 teaspoon of curry powder (or curry paste)
1 tin of sardines in oil
1 handful of pre-cooked rice (or crumbled crackers)

rj_kari_sud.source: Original Bivaska recipe, inspired by Uncharted and Far Cry. Unofficial: Bivaska is not affiliated with or endorsed by any publisher of the games mentioned

rj_biscuits_abri.intro: Concentrated carbs to replace bread gone soft with damp.
etapes: The dough: mix flour, salt, bicarbonate and fat in the mess tin. Add the water little by little until you get a firm but pliable dough.
The shaping: form walnut-sized balls and flatten them with your thumb into small, thick discs.
The setup: line the bottom of the cold mess tin with foil and put the biscuits on it.
The steam: close the lid tightly, with a heavy stone on top, and put the mess tin on very gentle embers.
The cooking: 15 minutes covered. They rise a little and harden without burning. Delicious dipped in a broth.
attention: No foil? Fresh hazel or lime leaves will do, only if you recognise them with certainty.

recette.cuisson: In the mess tin (steamed under the lid)
ingredients: 80 g of wheat flour
2 tablespoons of water, more if needed
1 pinch of bicarbonate of soda (or baking powder)
1 pinch of salt
1 small knob of lard or oil

rj_biscuits_abri.source: Original Bivaska recipe, inspired by Fallout. Unofficial: Bivaska is not affiliated with or endorsed by any publisher of the games mentioned

rj_bouillie_necrophage.intro: A quick recharge after a long walk or a big climb.
etapes: The heating: heat the salted water until it starts to bubble.
The plunge: pour in the flakes all at once and stir straight away to avoid lumps.
The fusion: after 2 minutes, when the porridge thickens, add the pieces of bar.
The mixing: take it off the heat and stir until the chocolate and caramel marble the porridge.
The effect: a luxury dessert that recharges your vigour gauge.

ingredients: 40 g of fine oat flakes
1 chocolate bar (Snickers type) or cereal bar, in pieces
200 ml of water (or reconstituted milk)
1 pinch of salt

rj_bouillie_necrophage.source: Original Bivaska recipe, inspired by The Witcher. Unofficial: Bivaska is not affiliated with or endorsed by any publisher of the games mentioned

rj_crumble_balmora.intro: Fruit, nuts and sugar: warm comfort before the night.
etapes: The compote: in the bottom of your stainless-steel mug, put the diced fruit, honey and butter.
The reduction: put the mug on a hot stone or a grill above gentle embers. 10 minutes, stirring, until the fruit is translucent and caramelised.
The crumbling: in a bag or between your hands, crush the biscuits and nuts into coarse crumbs.
The lid: sprinkle these crumbs over the hot fruit, without stirring.
The finishing touch: leave another 3 minutes at the edge of the fire so the top turns crispy. With a teaspoon, under the shelter.
attention: A titanium or stainless-steel mug can go on the fire. Not a plastic or double-walled cup: it melts or can warp.

recette.cuisson: In the mug or mess tin (indirect fire)
ingredients: 1 apple or 1 pear in small dice
3 crackers or dry biscuits
1 handful of mixed nuts (almonds, hazelnuts, walnuts)
1 tablespoon of honey or sugar
1 small knob of butter

rj_crumble_balmora.source: Original Bivaska recipe, inspired by The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind. Unofficial: Bivaska is not affiliated with or endorsed by any publisher of the games mentioned

isolation_sol.intro: At night, it's the ground that steals most of your heat, not the air: your weight crushes the sleeping bag's insulation underneath you, so it no longer insulates. The mat is what insulates you from the ground, and its R-value says how much.
etapes: The R-value measures the mat's resistance to heat flow. The higher it is, the better you're insulated from the cold ground.
Since 2020, the major brands measure the R-value with the same method (ASTM F3340 standard). These values can be compared. The old “in-house” values can't.
R-values add up: an R 2 foam pad under an R 4 inflatable gives R 6. Put the foam underneath: it protects the inflatable from thorns and still insulates you if it punctures.
Guide for the night temperature: above 10 °C, R 2 is enough; 5 to 10 °C, aim for R 3; 0 to 5 °C, R 3.5 to 4; −5 to 0 °C, R 4.5; −10 to −5 °C, R 5.5; below that, R 6 and more.
Add about 1 if you feel the cold, and 1 more on wet ground or snow.

The sleeping bag completes it: its “comfort” temperature is where a person who feels the cold sleeps well, its “limit” temperature is where a warm sleeper sleeps curled up without feeling cold. Below the limit, there's a risk of hypothermia.

Without a good enough mat: a thick bed of very dry dead leaves or bracken (30 cm before compressing), conifer branches, your empty pack and your rope under your legs. Less effective than a real mat, but much better than nothing.
Use Bivaska's calculator (Learn > Field tools > R-value): it adds up your gear and compares it with the night forecast at your bivouac spot.
attention: An inflatable mat without inner insulation (about R 1) is freezing as soon as the night drops below 10 °C, even with a good bag.
A survival blanket laid on the ground hardly insulates from the cold ground at all: it blocks moisture, not conduction.
A wet sleeping bag loses much of its warmth, especially down: keep it dry in a dry bag.
isolation_sol.source: ASTM F3340 standard (measuring the thermal resistance of mats) and EN/ISO 23537 standards (sleeping bags). Written for Bivaska.

crise_72h.intro: In a major crisis (general power cut, flood, storm, accident), the emergency services can't help everyone at once. The European Union asks every household to be able to manage on its own for at least 72 hours.
etapes: Get informed: sign up to your country's alert system and find the official sources (Bivaska > Ready 72 h > Country).
Make a plan with your household: who to call, where to meet if separated, what to do about children at school and vulnerable people.
Build a stock to stay at home for 72 hours: water (3 L per person per day), food that can be eaten without cooking, light, radio, medicines, cash.
Separately, prepare a light evacuation bag, ready to grab if you're told to leave: papers, medicines, water, charger, clothes.
Build up your stock little by little, with each shop: no need to buy everything at once or expensive gear.
Rotate: use what is nearing its date and replace it. Bivaska reminds you of dates in the Stock tab.
Think of elderly, ill or lonely neighbours: in a crisis, mutual help saves lives.
attention: Keep the stock somewhere easy to reach, known to the whole household.
A kit forgotten at the back of the cellar is useless: check it twice a year, for example when the clocks change.
crise_72h.source: Written for Bivaska based on the recommendations of the European Commission (72 h self-sufficiency, 2026), the Belgian Crisis Centre and civil protection services. In a crisis, the authorities' instructions take precedence over this sheet.

crise_panne.intro: A long outage cuts the heating, the fridge, sometimes water, the mobile network and payments. The greatest danger often comes from makeshift solutions.
etapes: Unplug sensitive appliances (computer, TV) to avoid damage when the power comes back. Leave one lamp switched on so you know when it returns.
Keep the fridge and freezer closed: a full freezer stays cold for about 48 hours, half full for about 24 hours.
Listen to the battery radio for instructions. Save your phone: power-saving mode, low brightness, aeroplane mode when you don't need it.
If the cold sets in: gather in a single room, close the doors, pile on layers, blankets and a hat.
If a water cut is announced, fill bottles and the bath (for the toilet and hygiene, not for drinking).
Check on vulnerable neighbours and people who depend on a medical device.
attention: Never a barbecue, camping stove, brazier or generator indoors or in a garage: carbon monoxide kills without a smell. Headaches, nausea, drowsiness in several people at once: get into fresh air and call 112.
Candles: never unattended. Prefer torches.
crise_panne.source: Written for Bivaska based on the recommendations of the European Commission (72 h self-sufficiency, 2026), the Belgian Crisis Centre and civil protection services. In a crisis, the authorities' instructions take precedence over this sheet.

crise_inondation.intro: Water sometimes rises very fast, and the current carries away more than you think. The golden rule: never go into moving water.
etapes: As soon as there's an alert: move valuables, papers and medicines upstairs; keep your evacuation bag within reach.
If water threatens the house and it's safe to do so, turn off the electricity and gas.
If you're told to evacuate, leave at once by the route indicated. Tell your loved ones.
If you're trapped, go upstairs (not into an attic with no way out) and signal: torch, sheet at the window, whistle, 112.
Afterwards: only go back when the authorities allow it, don't switch anything back on before it's checked, throw away food that touched the water, and follow the instructions about tap water.
Take photos of the damage for the insurance before cleaning up.
attention: 15 cm of moving water is enough to knock an adult over, 30 cm to carry away a car. Don't walk or drive in a flooded area.
Never go down into a cellar or underground car park during a flood.
crise_inondation.source: Written for Bivaska based on the recommendations of the European Commission (72 h self-sufficiency, 2026), the Belgian Crisis Centre and civil protection services. In a crisis, the authorities' instructions take precedence over this sheet.

crise_tempete.intro: During a storm, most injuries are caused by falling trees, branches and objects blown by the wind.
etapes: Before: bring in or tie down anything that can blow away (garden furniture, bins, trampoline), close shutters and windows.
Stay indoors, away from windows. Postpone journeys.
Don't go into the forest or under trees, and don't bivouac: that's where the danger is greatest, even after the peak of the wind.
Afterwards: never touch a fallen power line, move away and call 112.
Report trees fallen on the road and help neighbours if it's safe.
attention: After a storm, broken branches can stay hanging in the trees and fall several days later.
crise_tempete.source: Written for Bivaska based on the recommendations of the European Commission (72 h self-sufficiency, 2026), the Belgian Crisis Centre and civil protection services. In a crisis, the authorities' instructions take precedence over this sheet.

crise_canicule.intro: Heat kills every summer in Europe, especially elderly people, babies, the sick and those who work outdoors.
etapes: Drink regularly without waiting to be thirsty. Avoid alcohol.
Close shutters and windows during the day, ventilate at night when it's cooler.
Cool down: showers, damp cloths, the coolest room, air-conditioned places.
Avoid effort during the hot hours. Check on lonely or elderly people at least once a day.
attention: Never leave a child, a vulnerable person or an animal in a car, even for a few minutes.
alerte: Hot, dry skin, confusion, feeling faint, very high temperature: this is heatstroke, a life-threatening emergency. Call 112 and cool the person while you wait.
crise_canicule.source: Written for Bivaska based on the recommendations of the European Commission (72 h self-sufficiency, 2026), the Belgian Crisis Centre and civil protection services. In a crisis, the authorities' instructions take precedence over this sheet.
